text: A speciall lycence for 14 yeares graunted to Thomas Toogood, gent., and James Hayes, esqre, their executors, administrators, & assignes, for the sole use, exercise, and benefitt, in all His Matie'3 dominions of severall new invencons, by them found out, for the making of shipps to saile without the assistance of wynd or tyde ; and also a certeyne instrum4 for takeing of the way or course of any shipp with demonstrable exactnes ; and also a new invencon for the raising of water with springes, which may be of singular use for the draining of mynes ; with the usuall provisoes. Teste I£ apud Westmr, Augusti, 15 Car 2di. By writt of privy seale.

A grant unto James Harris, of Saint Mildreds Court, in the city of London, tea dealer, for his invtd "Improvement in the manufacture of shoes for horses and other cattle"; to hold, &c ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto William Gilbert Elliott, of Blisworth, in the county of Northampton, gentleman, for " Improvements in the manufacture of bricks, tiles, and pipes and other articles from plastic materials"; a communication ; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto John Eginton, of Birmingham, in the county of Warwick, engraver, of his new method of making buttons and button moulds of wood ; to hold to him, his executors, administors, and assigns, within England, W ales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westminster, the — day of January, in the year last above. By writt, &c.

A grant unto Edward Ives Fuller, of Margaret Street, Cavendish Square, in the county of Middlesex, carriage builder, and George Tabernacle, of Mount Row, Westminster Road, in the county of Surrey, coach-iron founder, for their invention of " Certain improvements in metallic springs for carriages"; 6 months.

Edward Nelthorpe, of London, merchant, haveing with great labour and expence invented and found out a certaine engine or mill for the hulling of black peppr and barley, being never yet used by any butt himselfe, His Made, att his speciall instance & nominacon, is pleased to graunt to Charles Milson, of London, merchant, lycence to use itt, & all the benefit hereby arrissing ; to hold to him the said Milson, his executors & assignes, for 14 years according to the statute ; and with clauses & non obstantes usuall in graunts of like nature. Teste apud Westm, 14° die February, anno sup dco. By writt.
A grant unto Louis Leconte, of Paris, now residing in Leicester Square, in the county of Middlesex, gentleman, for his invention of "Improvements in constructing fire proof buildings 6 months.

A grant unto Peter Kagenbusch, of Wctter-on-Rhur, in Westphalia, in the kingdom of Prussia, dyer, now residing in the parish of Lyth, in the county of York, for his invention of " Certain improvements in the treatment of the alum rock or schist, and in the manufacture and application of the products derived therefrom "; 6 months.

A grant unto Frank Hills, of Deptford, in the county of Kent, manufacturing chemist, for his invention of " Certain improvements in the construction of steam boilers and of locomotive engines"; 6 months.

A grant unto William Cooke, of Greenwich, in the county of Kent, esq1", for his invd improvements in the art of making and working ploughs of any kind or description ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and asss, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within two calendar months from the date thereof. By writ, &c.

A spiall priviledge graunted to His Ma1'3 servant Will'm Conneldon & his assignes, for 21 yeares, wthin England & Wales, to sett up, make, & put in use a furnace or furnaces, by him invented, for the moultinge of lead in greate quantities, & all other things of what nature soever wch are to be used to that purpose, & all engines, instruints, & devises whatsoever to the purposes aforesaid whereof he hath byn the first inventor. The same to be done wth seacoles & other fewell, not beinge woode, wth power to sell anie such furnaces, engines, or instruments to anie His Mal's subite, wth a phibicon to all others to imitate the said invencon without the license of the patentee, upon paine of forfeiture of anie such furnaces or engines, the one moytie whereof to be to His Matie th' other to the patentee. Paying therefore yearly into the receipt of excheqr, during the said terme, xijd for every tonn of lead to be moulten as aforesaid. And the patentee shall within 3 monthes next ensuinge, and all others wch by his license shall put in use the said invencon shall, within 3 monthes next after they shall beginne to practise the same, enter into several bonds to His Mal's use of 200u a peece for the making of a true accompt twise a yeare in the Co1 of Excheqr, & for the payment of the somes of money thereupon to become due accordinglie, or upon default thereof the gr1 to be voyd. Provided that if anie tyme his invencon shal be found to be piudicial to the comonwealth that then, upon significacon thereof under the hands of anie sixe of the Privy Councell, this gr* to be voyd. Teste 20° Septembf pd. p bfe &c.

A grant unto Thomas Machell, of Great Ryder Street, in the parish of S* James, West1-, in the coy of Midx, surgeon, for his invtd u Improved method of applying, for medicinal purposes, the agency of atmospheric air, liquid, or gaceous substances to the external surface and to some of the internal cavities and passages of the human body ; and for the more convenient and useful mode of employing oil and spirits, on similar principles, in lamps and other luminous apparatus " ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Onesiphorus Paul, of Woodchester, in the county of Gloucr, clothier, of his new invented method of preparing cloths intended to be dyed scarlett, so as more effectually to ground the colours and preserve their beauty, & other purposes therein mentioned ; to hold to him, his execis, admrs, and assignes, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute in that behalf ; with the like clause as next above. Witness His Matie at Westmr, the 19th day of March, in the year above. By writt, &c.

A grant unto Richard Archibald Brooman, of Fleet Street, in the city of London, gent", for " A thread made from a substance not hitherto applied to that purpose ; and also the application of it to the manufacture of piece goods, ribbons, paper, and other articles "; being a communication ; 6 months. /

A grant unto Charles Wyatt, of Birmingham, in the county of Warwick, merchant, of his new invented method of making and manufacturing pipes and spouts for conveying water and other liquids, and for making and manufacturing troughs and cistern heads for receiving or holding water from the roofs of buildings, and applicable to other purposes, of materials not heretofore used and applied to and for such purposes ; to hold to him, his exors, adniors, & asss, within Engd, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon- Tweed for the term of 14 yrs pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inrol the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at West1-, the 11th day of May, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Joshua Bates, of Bishopsgate Street, in the city of London, merchant, for " An improved method of condensing aeriform substances and refrigerating fluids "; being a communication from a foreigner residing abroad ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Joseru MAximinian Rirrer von Winiwarrer, of Surrey Street, Strand, in the county of Middlesex, doctor of law, for “ Certain improvements in the locks of fire-arms and cannon, and in gun matches, or in the mode of igniting gunpowder used in guns, and in machinery for manufacturing the same”; 6 months ; a communication, o D

A grant unto John Payne, of the city of London, merchant, his execre, admrs, & assignes, of the sole use & benefit of his invencon of a new & more advantageous method of expanding fluids, which being conveyed into a proper ignifyed vessel or vessels contrived for that purpose, are imediately rarifyed into an elastick impelling force sufficient to give mocon to hydraulopneumatical & other ingines for raising water and other uses ; and also in brewing and distilling by a new form or make of the boyler, still, evaporating vessel or vessels, & other contingencies thereunto belonging ; to hold the same within England, Wales, & town of Berwick upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years ; and also a clause for obliging him particularly to describe the nature of his invencon, by an instrument under his hand & seal, to be inrolled in His Matie's High Court of Chancery within two calendar months from the date of his intended grant, as has been frequently done in like cases. Witness Caroline, Queen of Great Britain, &c, at Westmr, as next above. By writt, &c.
A grant unto Thomas French Berne r, of Morton Hall, in the county of Norfolk, esquire, for his invention of "Certain improvements in cartridges"; 6 months.

A grant unto James Robson, of Dover, in the county of Kent, engineer, for his invention of "A new and improved instrument to be used in crushing or expressing oil from vegetable and other substances, and in making oil cake; and which instrument is applicable to the moulding, pressing, and manufacturing the same and other articles from plastic materials "; 6 months.

A grant unto Joseph Conrad Marie Baron de Liebhabeh, of Paris, in the kingdom of France, for "Improvements in blasting rocks and other mineral substances for mining and other purposes, and in apparatus t" be used in such works "; being a communication ; 6 months.

A grant unto Richard Garrett, of Leiston Works, near Saxmundham, in the county of Suffolk, agricultural implement manufacturer, for his invention of " Improvements in the construction of horse hoes, scarifiers, drag rakes, and drills for cultivating land "; 6 months.

A grant unto Edwj Weeks, of Llaveny Hall, in the parish of Henlau and county of Denbigh, in North Wales, gardener, for his invd and brought to perfection a forcing frame, on a new and improved construction, for raising and forcing of cucumbers, melons, strawberries, and various other fruits and plants which require the application of artifical heat to rear or ripen the same ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Harrison Grey Dyar, of N° 286, Regent Street, Oxford Street, in the county of Middlesex, gentleman, and John Chisholm, of Pomeroy Street, Old Kent Road, in the county of Surrey, manufacturing chemist, for their invention of "Improvements in obtaining sulphur from pyrites or certain native sulphuretts "; 6 months.

A grant unto Thomas Cobb, of Calthorpe House, near Bradbury, in the county of Oxford, esq., for his invented or found out " Certain improvements in the manufacture of paper intended to be applied to the covering of walls or the hanging of rooms, and in the apparatus for effecting the same " ; to hold, &c ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Roberts, of Wood Street, Cheapside, engineer, and George Upton, of Queen Street, Cheapside, oil merchant, both in the city of London, for their invented " Certain improvements on argand and other lamps "; to hold, &c ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto William Lowtiiee, of Hatton Garden, in the county of Middx, esq1", of his new invented medicine, which being made into powders are an effectual cure for all nervous & paralitick disorders, & chymically made into drops arc an imediatc cure for nervous & other pains & weaknesses ; to hold to him, his execrs, admrs, & assigns, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, and His Matie's colonies and plantacons abroad, for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within 4 kalendar months from the date hereof. Witness His Matie at Westm1", the 12th day of November, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Henry Gilbert, of Marina, St. Leonards, surgeon, for his invention of "Improvements in apparatus for holding sacks, to facilitate the filling them with corn or other materials "; 6 months.

A grant unto John Ramsbottom, of New Mills, in the county of Derby, engraver, for his invention of " Certain improvements in machinery or apparatus for measuring and registering the flow of water and other fluids or vapours ; which machinery or apparatus is also applicable to registering the speed of and distance run by vessels in motion ; and also for obtaining motive power and other similar purposes"; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto John Evans the younger, of Moreton Mills, near Wallingford, in the county of Berks, paper maker, for his invtd " Certain improvements on steam engines"; to hold, &c ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto William Fothergill Cooke, of Breeds Place, Hayings, in the county of Sussex, esquire, for his invention of " Improvements in giving signals and sounding alarms at distant places by means of elastic currents transmitted through metallic circuits "; 6 months.

A grant unto Richard Abbey, of Walthamstow, in the county of Essex, gentleman, for his invented " A new mode of preparing the leaf of a British plant for producing a healthy beverage by infusion "; to hold, &c ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Gerard Andrew Arney, of Mare Street, Hackney, in the county of Middlesex, gentleman, for his invention of " Improvements in the preparation of gelatine ; and improvements in fining or clarifying liquids"; 6 months.
A grant unto GrorGre Gwynne, of Sussex Square, in the county of Middlesex, esquire, for his invention of “ Improvements in the manufacture of sugar”; 6 months; colonies.

A grant unto William Norris, of Alston, in the county of Cumberland, land surveyor, for his invention of "Certain improvements in the manufacture of combs "; being a communication from a foreigner residing abroad.

A grant unto Alexander Cummino, watchmaker, of his new invented watercloset, which he apprehends will be of great publick utility ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within four calendar months from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westmr, the 11th day of November, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Dennis McCarthy, of the parish of Sl James's, Clerkenwell, in the county of Miditx, esq1', of his new invented composicon or cement called pietra cotta; to hold to him, his exors, admrs, & assigns, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, and also in His Matie's colonies & plantacons abroad, for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within 4 kalendar months from the date hereof. Witness His Matie at Westm1', the 6th day of March, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Nathaniel Matiieav, of Wern Tremadoc, in the county of Carnarvon, quarry proprietor, for his invention of " An apparatus for cutting or dressing slates into various shapes and sizes"; 2 months; colonies.
A grant unto Franz Anton Bernhardt, of Upper Montague Street, Montague Square, architect, for his invention of " Certain improvements in By writ, &c. warming and airino; buildings": six months.

A grant unto Richard Archibald Brooman, of the firm of J. C. Robertson and Company, of 166, Fleet Street, in the city of London, patent agent, for " Improvements in the manufacture of manure "; a communication ; 6 months.

A grant unto Michael Melnzies, esqre, of his new invented machine for carrying coals from the coal walls where they are dugg to the bottom of the pitt or shaft, and from the mouth of the pitt or shaft to the heaps, and for several other purposes therein particularly menconed ; to hold to him, his execrs, admrs, & assignes, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon- Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute in that behalf ; with a clause to inroll as next above. Witness His Matie at Westm1, the 9th day of Febry, in the year above. By writt, &c.

A grant unto John White, of New Compton Street, Soho, in the coy of Midx, gentleman, for his invented new and improved method of making candles ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within two calendar months from the date thereof: By writ, &c.

A grant unto James Baird, of Gartsherrie, in the parish of Old Monkland, in the county of Lanark, in Scotland, iron master, and Alexander Whit flaw, of Gartsherrie Iron Works, parish and county aforesaid, manager of said works, for their invention of "Improvements in the method or process of manufacture of iron"; 6 months.
A grant unto William Brindley, of Twickenham, papier-mache manufacturer, for his invention of improvements in the manufacture of waterproof paper "; 6 months.

A grant unto Tuomas WiLson, of Bishop Wearmouth, in the county of Durham, engineer, and RowLanp Burpon, of Castle Eden, in the said county, esquire, for their new invented methods of uniting, combining, and connecting the metallick patent blocks of the said Rowland Burdon for the construction of arches ; to hold to them, their eXors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-T weed, for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. W. H. M. at Westm’, the 234 day of July, in the year above. By writ, &°.

A grant unto George Forrester, of Vauxhall Foundry, Liverpool, in the county of Lancaster, civil engineer, for his invented " Certain improvements in wheels for carriages and machinery, which improvements are applicable to other purposes "; to hold, &° ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Dickins, esqr, his extors, admrs, & assigns, of the sole use and benefit of his new invented machine & new method by floats for raising great quantities of water to supply cities & towns, to water lands and gardens, for draining mines & fenny lands, for moving severall sorts of mill work, for moving ships & other vessels, and for severall other usefull purposes; to hold & exercise the same within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed and in your MajtL's plantacons in America, during the term of 14 years according to the statute in such case made and provided. Teste I£ apd Westm, 26° die Febvi-i, anno gd. p bre, &c.

A grant unto Edward Charles Howard, of Westbourn Green, in the county of Middx, for his invented process for preparing and refining sugars ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within 6 calendar months from the date thereof. By writ, &c.

A grant unto James Carpenter, of Willenhall, in the parish of Wolverhampton, in the county of Stafford, and John Young, of Wolverhampton aforesaid, locksmiths, for their invented " Certain improvements on locks and other securities, applicable to doors and other purposes "; to hold, &c ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto MarrHew Murray, of Leeds, in the county of York, engineer, for his new invented new combined steam engines, for producing circular powers, and certain machinery thereunto belonging, applicable to the drawing of coals, ores, and all other minerals from mines; and for spinning cotton, flax, tow, and wool, or for any other purpose requiring circular power ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within four calendar months from the date thereof. W.H. M. at Westm', the 28t day of June, in the year above. By writ, &*.
A grant unto Louis Arnier, of Rue du Loisir, Marseilles, in France, engineer, for his invention of " Certain improvements in steam boilers"; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto Aaron Jennens and John Betteridge, both of Birmingham, in the county of Warwick, manufacturers and japanners in ordinary, for their invented "Certain improvements in the method or methods of preparing and working pearl shell into various forms and devices, for the purpose of applying it into ornamental uses in the manufacture of japan ware and of other wares and articles to which the same can be applied "; to hold, &c ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Edward Heard, of Devonshire Street, Vauxhall Road, in the parish of Lambeth and county of Surrey, chemist, for his invented " Certain improvement or improvements in illumination or producing artificial light"; to hold, & ; six months. By writ, &c.
A grant unto Roperr Grirrirus, of Birmingham, in the county of Warwick, for his invention of “ Improvements in machinery for making rivet screw blanks and bolts”; six months. By writ, &.

A grant unto Colin Mather, of Sal ford, in the county of Lancaster, machine maker, and Ernest Rolffs, of Cologne, in the kingdom of Prussia, gentleman, for their invention of " Certain improvements in printing, damping, stiffening, opening, and spreading woven fabrics"; 6 months.

A grant unto Joseph Johnson, of Huddersfield, in the county of York, bricklayer, and Joe Cliffe, of the same place, iron founder, for their invention of" Improvements in furnaces, or in the means of consuming smoke "; 6 months; colonies.

A grant unto John Bradford Furnival, of Street Ashton, in the county of Warwick, farmer, for " Improvements in evaporating fluids, applicable to the manufacture of salt, and to other purposes where evaporation of fluids is required "; 6 months.

A grant unto Edward Ludlow, of Walworth, in the county of Surry, and Ann Wilcox, of the city of London, for their new invented playing cards, to be named " brilliant new invented knights' cards "; to hold to them, their exors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. W. H. M. at Westm1', the 20th day of Dec1, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A spiall priviledge graunted to Sir Theodore de Mayerne, kt, and Thomas Cademan, dcor in physicke, and their assignes, for the terme of 14 yeares next ensuing (wthin England and Wales), to exSsise and putt in practise the mistery and art of distilling strong waters and making vinegars of cider, perry, and buck or French wheate, whereof they have byn the first inventors — paying the yearely rent of xn, with prohibition of exportacon of buck or French wheate wthout licence from His Matv; wth a proviso that if this graunt is contrary to lawe or mischeivous to the state or gerklly inconvenient this graunt to be voide. Teste apud Westm1, xxv° Marcii, anno pd. p bre &c.

A grant unto James Deakin, of Sheffield, in the county of York, and Thomas Deakin, merchants and manufacturers of hardware, and partners , for their invented ''Certain methods of making, from horns and hoofs of animals, various articles, namely, handles of knives, handles and knobs of drawers and other parts of cabinet and household articles, curtain rings, bell pulls, door handles and knobs, key hole escutcheons or coverings, and door and window shutter finger plates, knobs, and handles ; all or any of which articles are to be so made of one or more piece or pieces of horn or hoof, of any shape or device, plain or ornamental, or inlaid or conjoined with any kind of metal or other material"; to hold, &c ; two months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Dickson, of Brook Street, Holborn, in the county of Middlesex, engineer, for his invention of " Improvements in rotatory engines and boilers, in stopping railway carriages, and in machinery for propelling vessels ; part of which improvements are applicable to propelling air and gases "j 6 months.
A grant unto William Gibbons, of Corbyn's Hall, near Dudley, in the county of Worcester, for his invention of " Certain improvements in trussing beams and girders"; 6 months.

A grant unto Epmunp Morewoop, of Thornbridge, in the county of Derby, merchant, and GrorGE Rocers, of Sterndale, in the same county, sentleman, for their invention of “Improvements in the manufacture of iron into sheets, plates, or other forms, in coating iron, and in preparing iron for coating, and other purposes”; 6 months.

A grant unto Martin Triewald, of Newcastle-upon-Tyne, gent., his execls, adm1'3, 8c assignes, of the sole use 8c benefit of his new invencon of a certain engine or machine for drawing water out of mines and collyeries by the power of the atmosphere, within England, Wales, 8c town of Berwickupon-Tweed for 8c during the term of 14 years according to the statute in such case made 8c provided. Teste J$ apd Westih, 29° die Junij, anno pd. p bre, 8cc.

A grant unto Josefh Hughes, of Whitehall Mills, Chapel-le-Frith, in the county of Derby, paper maker, for his invention of " Certain improvements in the method or process of manufacturing paper"; 6 months.
A grant unto John Hackett, of Leicester, for his invention of "Improvements in the manufacture of pill boxes"; (} months.

A grant unto Adolpiius Henri Erneste Ragon, of Great Portland Street, in the county of Middlesex, professor of literature, for " Improvements in the manufacture of glass, and in the production of other vitrified matters applicable to architectural purposes."

A grant unto Charles Claggett, from the city of Waterford, in Ireland, at present in the city of London, musick master, of his new improvements on the violin and other instruments played on finger boards, that render it almost impossible to stop or play out of time ; that the violin, &ca, will retain all former perfections ; and that these improvements, at the same time that they infinitely assist the very best performers, will save learners above four-fifths of their trouble and time ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and ass , within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years, pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within four calendar months from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westm1", the 7t!l day of December, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto James Keir, of Birmingham, in the county of Warwick, gentleman, of his new invented compound metal, capable of being forged when red hot or when cold, and more lit for making of bolts, nails, and sheathing for ships than any metal heretofore used for those purposes ; and also for various other purposes where other metals have been used, which he apprehends will be of great public utility ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, & ass% within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within 4 calendar months from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westrn1-, the 10th day of Dec1-, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Silvester, of West Bromwich, in the county of Stafford, whitesmith, for his invention of "Certain improvements in the arrangement and construction of apparatus for hanging and closing doors "; 6 months.

A grant unto Benjamin Robinson and Francis Hanksbee, of the City of London, esqrs, their execrs, adm1"8, and assignes, of the sole use and benefit of their new invencon of preserving plank and sheathing of ships, which will not only effectually prevent the worms and other shell insects from eating and fouling their bottomes, but enable the ships so sheathed, Oven in their long voyages, to outsail any other ships of the same burthen and forme ; to hold and exercise the same within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years according to the statute in such case made and provided. Teste ^ apd Westm, 9° die Maij, ami f)d. p bre, &c.

A grant unto Richard Roberts, of the Globe Works, Manchester? in the county of Lancaster, engineer, for his invention of " Certain improvements in and applicable to clocks and other time-keepers, in machinery or apparatus for winding clocks and hoisting weights, and for effecting telegraphic communications between distant clocks and places otherwise than by electro-magnetism"; 6 months.
A grant unto Samuel Mokand, of Manchester, in the county of Lancaster, merchant, for his invented or found out " An improved stretching machine"; to hold, &c ; six months. By writ, &c.
A grant unto Joseph Bentiiam, of Bradford, in the county of York, weaver, for his invention of "Improvements in weaving1'; six months.
A grant unto Henry Needham, of Vim1 Street, Piccadilly, in the city of Westminster, gun maker, for his invention of " Certain improvements in lire-arms"; 6 months.
A grant unto Thomas Forsyth, of Salford, in the county of Lancaster, engineer, for his invention of Certain improvements in machinery for making bricks and tiles "; 6 months.

A grant unto Stephen Perry, of Wilmington Street, Wilmington Square, gentleman, and Edward Massey senior, of King Street, Clerkenwell, watcli manufacturer, and Paul Joseph Gauci, of North Crescent, Bedford Square, artist, all in the county of Middlesex, for their invention of " Certain improvements in pens and penholders": six months. By writ. &c.

A grant unto Joseph Weld, of Pylewell House, in the county of Southampton, esquire, for his invtd and brought to perfection " A machine for separating corn, grain, and seeds from the straw "; to hold, &c ; 2 months. 5 By writ, &c.

A grant unto Weston Tuxford, of Boston, in the county of Lincoln, for his invention of " Improvements in machinery for crushing or pressing land, and for shaking straw ; also improvements in applying steam power to agricultural machinery "; 6 months.

A grant unto Daniel Maun sell, of Sion Row, Clifton, near Bristol, in the county of Somerset, esquire, of his new invented horizontal windmill, upon entire new principles, for grinding corn, and various other purposes ; to hold to him, his executors, administrators, and assigns, within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inrol the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westminster, the 8th day of December, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Edward Newman Fourdrinier, of Cheddleton, in the county of Stafford, paper manufacturer, for his invention of "Improvements in apparatus to be used for raising and lowering weights from mines and other places "; 6 months.
